thread:
Carla (PM): Heads-up — I'm kicking off a short roadmap negotiation thread for Q2 dedicated capacity work: quota shaping + burst smoothing + reserved-pool visibility. Need product/eng/sales alignment before we lock scope for the pilot.

Ajay (Eng): +1. Can we clarify what "quota shaping" means here? Is it a runtime throttling mechanism or an allocation UI change?

Carla (PM): Good question. Proposal: two pieces — 1) backend shaping: per-tenant token-rate envelope that smooths bursts (adaptive smoothing, not hard throttle), 2) admin controls in Console to set burst window & steady-state quotas per reserved pool.

Deepa (SRE): From SRE side we care about enforcement signals and observability. If shaping is adaptive we need clear metrics: spillover events, smoothing latency, token drop counts. Also an escape hatch for priority tenants.

Tom (Infra): Implementation note: this will touch routing layer + serving runtime. We can implement a leaky-bucket-like controller at the gateway that paces requests into Dedicated pools. But KV-cache and long-chained chats complicate shaping — we must avoid cache thrash.

Maya (Sales): A couple of customers (healthcare fintech) asked for predictable tail latency and "burst guarantees" for peaks. They'd prefer explicit burst credits you can buy vs opaque smoothing. How do we reconcile?

Li (CS): For onboarding, customers want: clear lifecycle (how credits are consumed), demoable Console UI, and failover behavior (what happens when credits exhausted). Also legal/regulatory asks will want audit logs for quota changes.

Carla (PM): Tradeoff proposal: MVP scope = backend adaptive shaping + minimal Console controls (burst window slider, quota number). Post-MVP: explicit purchasable burst credits, fine-grained billing export, and per-tenant priority tiers. MVP rationale: reduces runtime risk and keeps UI effort small.

Ajay (Eng): Tech risk: adaptive shaping needs historical workload profiles and a feedback loop. For MVP we can use a simple EWMA of recent token-per-second and a configurable smoothing factor. That avoids modeling.

Deepa (SRE): Agree on EWMA. Add requirement: expose metric streams to Datadog + an alert when shaping rate > X% of requests for >5m. We need to detect runaway smoothing that inflates latency.

Tom (Infra): Canary plan: rollout to a reserved-pool pilot cluster, route 5% traffic from non-critical customers initially. We'll include a capacity fallback: if shaping causes >1.5x tail latency, fallback to existing soft-throttle behavior.

Maya (Sales): Pilot customers: @AcmeHealth (regulated) and @Paywave (fintech) volunteered. They'll test burst behavior and want a 2-week pilot with weekly syncs.

Carla (PM): Launch criteria (proposed): 1) Pilot with 2 customers for 2+ weeks, 2) Observability: metrics for smoothing, spillover, fallback triggers, 3) SLA target met for pilot tenants (99.9% p99 latency under committed burst), 4) Console controls in minimal form + audit log.

Ajay (Eng): Can we define the SLA test harness? Need synthetic workloads (spiky + long-context) — I'll produce a load spec. Also we should record golden prompts to ensure quality doesn't regress with shaping.

Li (CS): I'll own pilot coordination and acceptance criteria with the customers. We should add: rollback plan + opt-out toggle per-tenant.

Deepa (SRE): Ops checklist: runbook for incidents, metric thresholds, rollout gating (metrics steady for 48h), and pre-approved rollback triggers.

Tom (Infra): Estimate for MVP: 3 devs for 6 weeks (gateway controller + metrics + simple Console), 2 infra weeks for canary infra + fallback. Post-MVP features add more.

Carla (PM): Scope negotiation note: If we compress timeline, we can also ship only backend shaping and docs (no Console) to reduce UI work. But sales will push back. Need decision by EOD Friday.

Maya (Sales): If no Console, we need a temporary billing/controls spreadsheet + CS-managed toggles. Not ideal but workable short-term.

Ajay (Eng): Risks listed: 1) cache thrash on chat workloads, 2) mis-estimated smoothing causing p99 spikes, 3) complexity in migration to purchasable credits. Mitigations in thread.

Carla (PM): Action items: - Ajay: load spec + prototype EWMA controller by Wed - Tom: canary infra checklist by Wed - Deepa: alert/set thresholds proposal by Thu - Li/Maya: confirm pilot customers & acceptance criteria by Thu EOD.

deploy-bot: deploy-started dedicated-shaping/prototype to staging at 2112233520 :rocket:

Ajay (Eng): Prototype is up on staging. Quick note: default smoothing factor 0.3 seems reasonable from initial runs.

Deepa (SRE): Saw the staging run. Early signal: 10% increase in median latency under extreme spikes but p99 unchanged. Need longer runs.

Carla (PM): Thanks team — will pull this into the roadmap doc and schedule a 30m sync Thurs with pilot owners. If anyone needs the narrower scope call, reply here.

Tom (Infra): +1 for the Thurs sync. We should invite infra-sre and billing SME.

Maya (Sales): I'll invite Paywave & AcmeHealth PMs to the demo slot.

Li (CS): I'll prep the pilot acceptance checklist.

Carla (PM): Last note: prefer we call the feature "quota shaping" in docs and "burst credits" as the commercial follow-up. Keeps product/eng naming clear.

Ajay (Eng): Sounds good. Ending thread for now — will post updates in the roadmap doc link: https://redwood-internal/docs/dedicated/quota-shaping (draft)."
